item.title: Next Project: ESP32-S3 and a 4.2 Inch E-Ink Display
item.description: After designing a case for my ESP32 WiFi scanner I’ve picked up some new parts to play with: a WeAct Studio ESP32-S3-N16R8 dev board — 16MB of flash and 8MB of PSRAM, dual USB-C, RGB status LED, sat in a little printed case I already had lying around — paired with a WeAct Studio 4.2 inch e-paper module, 400x300 resolution over a simple SPI header (GND, SDA, SCL, CS, D/C, RES, BUSY, VCC).

item.title: Designing and Printing a Case for My ESP32 WiFi Scanner
item.description: After designing my first shelf in TinkerCAD, I wanted a project that actually needed a proper enclosure rather than a mounting bracket. I’d been building a small self-contained WiFi scanner around this cheap ESP32 dev board — an ESP32 module with a built-in 1.14 inch LCD — paired with a small rechargeable battery, and it had been living on my desk as a loose tangle of board, wires and cells. Time to give it a case.
